name.text: Using trig substitution to evaluate an Integral

generalfeedback.text:
\( \text{In order to carry out trig substitution integrals, let's take a look at the information in the table below.} \)

\( \text{If you see }\)

\( \text{Use the following substitution}\)

\(\text{Where}\)

\(\text{So that,}\)

\(\sqrt{a^2-x^2}\)

\(x=a\sin(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\cos(\theta)d(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{a^2-x^2} = a\cos(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{a^2+x^2}\)

\(x=a\tan(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\sec^{2}(\theta)d(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{a^2+x^2} = a\sec(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{x^2-a^2}\)

\(x=a\sec(\theta)\)

\(dx=a\sec(\theta)\tan(\theta)d(\theta)\)

\(\sqrt{x^2-a^2} = a\tan(\theta)\)

In this case, we’ll need the following trig substitution.

\(t= {@coef@}\). Then \( dt={@dif_coef@} \,d(\Theta) \)

Let's first use the substitution to eliminate the root, and considering the fact that we are doing an indefinite integral we will assume that the tangent is positive.

\( \begin{align} {@expr1@} & = \left(\sqrt{{@coeff_tsquared*t^2-const@}} \right)^{@num@}\\ & = \left( \sqrt{{@const@}\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})-{@const@}} \right)^{{@num@}}\\ & = \left( {@sqrt(const)@}\sqrt{\tan^2{@var_theta@}} \right)^{@num@} && \text{since, } \tan^{2}({@var_theta@}) = \sec^{2}({@var_theta@}) - 1 \\ & ={@(sqrt(const))^num@}\tan^{{@num@}}({@var_theta@}) && \text{since, } \tan({@var_theta@}) > 0 \end{align} \)

Now let's do the actual substitution.

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle\int{@func@}dt & = \displaystyle \int {@coeff_tcubed@} \left( {@coef@} \right)^{3} \cdot {@(sqrt(const))^num@}\tan^{{@num@}}({@var_theta@}) \cdot \left( {@ dif_coef@} \right) \, d(\Theta) \\ & = \displaystyle \int {@expr7@} \, d(\Theta) \\ & = \displaystyle \int {@expr8@} {\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})} \, d(\Theta) && \text{since, } \sec^{2}({@var_theta@})= \tan^{2}({@var_theta@}) + 1. \end{align} \)

Now, let \(u=\tan({@var_theta@})\). Then \(du =\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})d{@var_theta@}\), and so \( d{@var_theta@}=\frac{du}{\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})} \)

Therefore:

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle\int{@func@}dt & = \displaystyle \int {@expr8@} {\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})} \, d(\Theta) \\ & = \displaystyle \int \left({@expr9@}\right) {\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})} \, \frac{du}{{\sec^{2}({@var_theta@})}} \\ & = \displaystyle \int \left( {@expr9@} \right) \, du \\ & = \displaystyle \int \left( {@expr10@} \right) \, du && \text{since, } u=\tan({@var_theta@})\\ & = \displaystyle {@expr11@} \\ & = \displaystyle {@expr12@} && \text{because, } u=\tan({@var_theta@})\\ & = \displaystyle {@expr13@} && \text{since, } \tan({@var_theta@})={@expr_tan@}\\ \end{align} \)

Therefore,

\[\displaystyle\int{@func@}dt = \displaystyle {@expr13@} \]
